structure_explanation.en: お手上げ ('hands up') is an idiom meaning 'to be at a loss, to have no way out'. まったく intensifies it affirmatively ('completely'), and だ is the plain copula. Here まったく reinforces the assertion; it is not the negative まったく…ない pattern.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: お手上げ ('mãos ao alto') é uma expressão idiomática que significa 'estar sem saída, não ter o que fazer'. まったく a intensifica de forma afirmativa ('completamente'), e だ é a cópula simples. Aqui まったく é reforço de afirmação, não o padrão negativo まったく…ない.

objections.objection: This is a gen=false (real Tatoeba) record, so the source English is Layer A and must be left untouched. The patch writes translation.en = "I'm completely at a loss." — a newly authored English string replacing the Tatoeba-sourced en the op quotes as "everything's a little crazy". Fixing a bad Japanese/English Tatoeba pairing by rewriting the authoritative en destroys provenance; the mismatch should be recorded/quarantined (or the pairing dropped), not silently overwritten. Note also that the diff's "before" shows no en at all, so the apply step is inventing a Layer-A field value.
objections.auditor_hint: Leave the Layer A source en unchanged; quarantine the record as a mis-linked Tatoeba pair instead of authoring a replacement en.

current.jp: ハウスダストにアレルギーがあります。
current.kana: はうすだすとにあれるぎーがあります。

structure_explanation.en: The structure is [noun + に] + [noun + が + あります], that is, the pattern ～があります ('to exist/there is', and by extension 'to have'). ハウスダスト (house dust) takes に to indicate the target of the allergy ('to/against'). アレルギー (allergy) is marked by が as that which exists, and あります (polite form of ある) affirms the existence. The target があります appears clearly here.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A estrutura é [substantivo + に] + [substantivo + が + あります], ou seja, o padrão ～があります ('haver/existir', e por extensão 'ter'). ハウスダスト (poeira doméstica) recebe に para indicar o alvo da alergia ('a/contra'). アレルギー (alergia) é marcado por が como aquilo que existe, e あります (forma polida de ある) afirma a existência. O alvo があります aparece claramente aqui.

translation_literal.en: To house dust, an allergy (subject) exists.

translation.en: translation.en = "He is allergic to house dust." (restore Layer-A verbatim) and translation.pt-BR = "Ele tem alergia a poeira doméstica."

gloss.en: to exist, to be (inanimate things); here 'to have'

note.en: conjunctive stem (あり) of ある, linked to ます
note.pt-BR: raiz conjuntiva (あり) de ある, ligada a ます

note.en: auxiliary ます in the affirmative present, forming あります
note.pt-BR: auxiliar ます no presente afirmativo, formando あります

current.jp: チェスを一番どうですか。
current.kana: ちぇすをいちばんどうですか。

structure_explanation.en: Invites someone to play chess: チェス is the object marked by を, and どうですか ('how about it?') makes the invitation. 一番 here is NOT the adverbial/superlative 一番: it is the numeral 一 plus the counter 番 used for games and bouts, so チェスを一番 = 'one game of chess' (the same slot as ビールを一杯どうですか, 'how about a glass of beer?'). The listed target pattern therefore does not apply here.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase convida a jogar xadrez: チェス ('xadrez') é o objeto marcado por を, e どうですか ('que tal?') faz o convite. 一番 aqui NÃO é o 一番 adverbial/superlativo: é o numeral 一 + o contador 番, usado para partidas/rodadas, então チェスを一番 = 'uma partida de xadrez' (mesma estrutura de ビールを一杯どうですか, 'que tal um copo de cerveja?'). Logo, o padrão-alvo não se aplica.

translation_literal.en: Chess (object), one bout, how is it? (= how about it?)
translation_literal.pt-BR: Xadrez [obj.], uma partida, como é? (= que tal?)

translation.pt-BR: Que tal uma partida de xadrez?

gloss.en: one game, a round (numeral 一 + counter 番 for bouts/matches)
gloss.pt-BR: que tal uma partida/uma rodada (lit. 'número um', aqui no sentido de jogar uma vez)

role.en: interrogative adverb (head of どうですか)
role.pt-BR: advérbio interrogativo (núcleo de どうですか)

current.jp: その橋は長さが１００メートルある。
current.kana: そのはしわながさがひゃくめーとるある。

structure_explanation.en: The sentence uses the double-subject structure typical of Japanese: その橋は marks the bridge as the general topic ('as for that bridge') and 長さが marks 'the length' as the specific subject that receives the measurement. The final verb ある ('to exist/there is') indicates that 'there is' 100 meters of length, that is, the bridge 'has' that length. 100メートル is the measured quantity.
structure_explanation.pt-BR: A frase usa a estrutura de duplo sujeito típica do japonês: その橋は marca a ponte como tópico geral ('quanto àquela ponte') e 長さが marca 'o comprimento' como o sujeito específico que recebe a medida. O verbo final ある ('existir/haver') indica que 'há' 100 metros de comprimento, ou seja, a ponte 'tem' esse comprimento. 100メートル é a quantidade medida.

translation_literal.en: As for that bridge, its length is/has 100 meters.
translation_literal.pt-BR: Quanto àquela ponte, o comprimento, 100 metros, existe/há.

translation.pt-BR: Aquela ponte tem 100 metros de comprimento.

note.pt-BR: forma de dicionário de ある

objections.objection: Pre-existing (identical in before), but it survives a patch that specifically rewrites this record's kana/romaji/reading, so the after-state still fails the jp/kana/token consistency invariant. tokens[0]='長'(なが) and tokens[1]='さ'(さ) are orphan duplicates of tokens[5]='長さ' prepended to the array: concatenating token readings yields 'ながさそのはしわながさがひゃくめーとるある。' against kana 'そのはしわながさがひゃくめーとるある。'. Both orphans carry null gloss/role. They must be dropped and the array reindexed - note this also shifts the op indices (その=2, １００=7) used by this diff.

current.jp: そして何時間もいっしょに話したからです。
current.kana: そしてなんじかんもいっしょにはなしたからです。

structure_explanation.en: そして opens the sentence as a connective ('and'), chaining it to the previous utterance. 何時間も uses も after 何時間 to emphasize a large amount ('for hours and hours'). いっしょに ('together') is adverbial. The ending 話したからです combines the verb 話した (past) + からです, which gives an explanation or reason ('it's because we talked...').
structure_explanation.pt-BR: そして abre a frase como conectivo ('e'), encadeando-a ao enunciado anterior. 何時間も usa も após 何時間 para enfatizar uma quantidade grande ('por horas e horas'). いっしょに ('juntos') é adverbial. O fecho 話したからです combina o verbo 話した (passado) + からです, que dá uma explicação ou motivo ('é porque conversamos...').

translation_literal.en: And, it's because we talked together for hours and hours.
translation_literal.pt-BR: E, quantas-horas até, juntos com, conversamos porque é.

translation.pt-BR: E porque conversamos juntos por horas a fio.

note.en: connective stem of 話す (話し), before the past た
note.pt-BR: raiz conjuntiva de 話す (話し), antes do passado た

note.en: past auxiliary た in 話した
note.pt-BR: auxiliar た de passado em 話した

gloss.en: is (explanatory copula, in からです)
gloss.pt-BR: é (cópula de explicação, em からです)

note.en: です in からです, giving the sentence a tone of reason/explanation
note.pt-BR: です em からです, dando a frase tom de motivo/explicação
